what: When the pointer is over a full-bleed video section, a 72px dark ink circle (inner 88% thin ring + 「Play」) rises in .4s, and every frame it follows the cursor late by 8% of the remaining distance (20px up and right of the cursor). Leaving the section turns it off in .2s, and pressing it fires an fx:play event — the view video larger button. On touch devices the circle stays in place (set by the consuming css) and only the circle is pressable.

options.dx: Px to the right of the cursor, default 20
options.[data-fx-part=disc]: Following circle (child) — if absent, nothing is hooked. The ring and text go inside the circle on the user side

from.where: index.html .tr-video + .tr-play.is-cursor (Play circle over the full-bleed video) — original p-index-video-play follows the cursor in gsap.ticker at a .08 ratio
index.html .rx-reel__follow — the big ‹Watch Reel› text over the showreel follows the cursor 10% per frame and scales .1 → 1 (lerp .1, difference-blend big text instead of a circle)

note: The original multiplies by .08 per frame, so it speeds up on high refresh rate screens. The part is tuned to one 60fps frame so the lag is the same on any screen. Opening the video large on press is up to the caller, who receives fx:play
